buisnesses. Exclude ETFs. And run everything through the frame work. Each should end with a
price and whether it did or did not pass the framework."*

*(Dated note 2026-10-05: the working rules below name v4.1's questions (Q1 to Q4 the gates, Q5 the price, six questions,
four verdicts). v5 governs from 2026-10-05 (`Framework/THE FRAMEWORK v5.md`): the price is Q7, the questions ahead of it
are Q1 to Q6 with their STOPs and weighings, and the box is IN, OUT or TOO HARD. The two requirements stand unchanged in
substance: a price either way, headed `COMPUTATION - NOT A CLEARANCE` when a STOP closed the file before Q7, and a plain

up to this date was made under them; the FOLD and the write-early protocol are read with this note.)*

**EVERY RUN IN THIS QUEUE MUST END WITH BOTH:**
1. **A PRICE.** If Q1-Q4 all show IN, the price band is a normal Q5 output. **If the file
   closes earlier, the price is still reported, headed `COMPUTATION - NOT A CLEARANCE`
   (operator rule 3), and it carries no entry language.** The operator gets a number either
   way; the framework's hard sequence is preserved by the heading, not by withholding it.
2. **A PASS/FAIL LINE**, stated plainly: which question closed the file, or that all six
   returned IN.

The guard caught a real finding: **owner earnings more negative each year than the whole common is quoted at.** The 1-for-10 reverse split (effective 2025-08-29, 8-K `0001811210-25-000022`) is real and bites in two other places: companyfacts' dei series carries the unadjusted pre-split counts (3,072,494,911 at 2025-07-30) beside the post-split ones, so the `a8bc84f` `share_count_shift()` returns **0.1308** and would have held the name as a "corporate action"; and **had any reader divided by that stale pre-split count, the yield would have been about -22.6%, inside the guard: a range guard on the quotient cannot tell a broken denominator from a business that consumes more than its market value, and for LCID the correct count is what tripped it.** The watchlist pricing script is not on disk (the HBB finding), so the triage's own count is reconstructed, not read. The run closed at Q2 on the business. For SOUN and BIRD, test all three readings (per-class or stale count, split, and the yield bound) before assuming any.*

**HOW A BANK IS RUN, FROM THE CORPUS - read before briefing one:**
- **Q3 becomes the deciding gate, not an overlay.** *"Because leverage of 20:1 magnifies the effects of
  managerial strengths and weaknesses, we have no interest in purchasing shares of a poorly-managed bank at
  a 'cheap' price. Instead, our only interest is in buying into well-managed banks at fair prices"*
  **[E3-29]**. This is the one place cheapness is ruled out as a remedy.
- **The named failure mode is conformity** - *"the tendency of executives to mindlessly imitate the behavior
  of their peers, no matter how foolish it may be to do so"* **[E3-02]**. Test what this bank did while its
  peers were lax.

  eighteen-year window contains both ends of **[E2-58]**'s *"ratio of supply-tight to

  homebuilder that adopted ASC 606 this way are not like-for-like**, because ~$30-45M a year of
  model-home spend moved out of OCF and into investing.

## THE WRITE-EARLY PROTOCOL - mandatory for every run in this queue
*Added 2026-09-02 after the fourth consecutive session-limit loss.*

**THE OBSERVED FAILURE MODE.** Runs die at the session limit **at the moment of writing the
file**, after the expensive work is already done. The last words before death, verbatim from
four separate agents:

> *"Now I'll write the run file."* (NKE) · *"Now let me build the full owner-earnings and
> decomposition arithmetic."* (DG) · *"Now let me start pulling primary data."* (ULTA) ·
> *"I'll continue reading the framework."* (QCOM)

Wave 1 lost four of six the same way; GM, OXY and PLAB survived **only because they had
already written partial files.** F, KR and AEO had to restart from nothing after 300k+ tokens
of research each. **The determinant of whether work survives is not how far the run got. It is
whether anything was on disk.**

**THE RULE, and it costs nothing.**

1. **Create the run file from the template BEFORE fetching anything.** First action, not last.
2. **Write each question's section AS SOON AS IT CLOSES.** Do not hold Q1 through Q4 in
   context to write them together at the end.
3. **Commit after every question**, or at minimum after Q2 and Q4. A dirty working tree is not
   a saved file.
4. **Write research to `Test Runs\_research <date> <TICKER>\` as it is gathered**, not at the
   end. The LSTR competitor row survived only because a sub-agent had written it out.

A run killed under this protocol loses **one question**. A run killed under the old habit loses
**everything**. This is the same discipline the framework already applies to evidence: **NOTHING
IS WRITTEN UNTIL ITS EVIDENCE EXISTS**, and its corollary, which this queue now adds: **nothing
is KNOWN until it is on disk.**

## CLAIM THE NAME AT DISPATCH, NOT AT FOLD - added 2026-09-19 after two agents ran AIG
**What happened.** Two agents were dispatched on AIG the same afternoon: one by the interactive session,
one by an unattended cycle. The second found the first had already committed **562 lines through the end of
Q2** into `Test Runs/2026-09-19 Run - AIG American International Group.md`, and refused to write to that
path, converting its work into
`Test Runs/_research 2026-09-19 AIG/REPLICATION - independent second run, findings owed to the AIG fold.md`.
**Only the write-early protocol, plus one agent committing first, prevented 562 lines being overwritten.**

**Two causes, one fixed in code and one fixed here.**
1. **The unattended cycle deleted a lock it did not hold.** `Screens/_daily/_overnight.ps1` removed the lock
   file in its `finally` block whatever PID was in it, so the 14:31 cycle released the interactive session's
   lock and the 15:31 cycle dispatched on an empty tree. **Fixed the same day: a cycle now releases the lock
   only if the lock holds its own PID, and traces the fact when it does not.**
2. **Nothing claimed a name until the fold.** The FOLD below records a name as taken only when its register
   entry is written, which is the END of a run of forty minutes or more. **A name is now claimed when the run
   file is created**, which the write-early protocol already requires in the first few tool calls - so
   **before starting any name, list `Test Runs/` for `*Run - <TICKER> *.md`, and if a file exists and was
   modified in the last 45 minutes, take a different name.** That test already existed for the unattended
   cycles; it is now a rule for every dispatcher, interactive sessions included.

**The replication was not wasted and it is not folded.** Its eight findings (an eleventh year of the
combined-ratio series, a proxy-against-10-K candor inconsistency, the retention test failing at $0.65 per
dollar, the cash-tax tell, and a below-gate floor computation) sit in the research folder, owed to whichever
session finishes the AIG fold. **Two gaps it raised in the insurer sector method are recorded there too:
float that has been reinsured away, and the multi-currency finding.**

## THE FOLD - what closing a run means, and it is not finished when the run file is
*Added 2026-09-07, after five runs were found missing from this file.*

**THE OBSERVED FAILURE MODE, and it is the mirror of the one above.** A run is written by an
agent; the FOLD is done by whoever is holding the session. When the run agent did its own
fold, the entry appeared here. When the main session did it, the entry went into
`Screens/2026-08-31 PREPPED READING LIST (operator lists).md` and **this file never learned
the run had happened.** Measured 2026-09-07: **AMAT and CRWD were recorded here because their
agents wrote them; TXN, QLYS, CERT, CRM and DAL were missing, and all five were still
UNSTRUCK in the tier-2 roster** - so the queue read as though five completed names were still
waiting. **The register that discharges the operator's instruction was the one being skipped.**

**THE RULE. A run is not closed until all six are done:**

1. **The entry in `## COMPLETED FROM THE QUEUE` above** - with the **price**, the **share
   count and the cover accession it came from**, the **cap**, the **sovereign**, and the
   **PASS/FAIL line naming which question closed the file.** This is where the operator's
   instruction of 2026-09-01 is actually discharged; the reading-list fold does not carry
   these fields.
2. **Strike the ticker in its tier roster** (`~~TICKER~~`). An unstruck name reads as unrun.
3. **The narrative fold** into `Screens/2026-08-31 PREPPED READING LIST (operator lists).md` -
   the findings, the refuted priors, the tooling defects.
4. **Arm the bands in `tools/alerts.json` and add the `PORTFOLIO.md` row** - **for
   gate-clearers only.** A name that failed at Q2 failed on the BUSINESS, and a price alert on
   it would be a category error; record the reversal condition in words instead (the QLYS
   ruling, 2026-09-07).
5. **`python tools/check_framework.py` must PASS** before the commit, not after.
6. **Commit WITH A PATHSPEC: `git commit -F <message-file> -- <path> <path> ...`.**
   *Corrected 2026-09-12. The rule this replaced said "commit your own files by name", and that was
   not enough.* **`git add mine && git commit` commits the WHOLE shared index**, so any file another
   session has staged goes into your commit under your title. Tested in two fresh repositories:
   `git add mine.txt && git commit` produced a commit containing `mine.txt` AND `theirs.txt`; `git
   commit -- mine.txt` produced one containing only `mine.txt`, and left the other session's staged
   file untouched in the index. **This is the root cause of all six crossings recorded in this tree**
   (the ORLY-titled INOD commit, the PLPC commit carrying my queue backfill, the DAL message on CRM's
   edits, and SWK's staged deletion inside the ACMR commit among them). Staging by name only chose
   what YOU added; it never excluded what someone else had. **A pathspec on the commit itself is the
   only thing that isolates it.** Crossings already made stay recorded, never rebased (operator rule 6).

*Dated note, 2026-09-21, added by the USNA fold beside step 1 rather than rewriting it (operator
rule 6):* ***WRITE THE REGISTER ENTRY BY LINE, NOT BY STRING.*** *A `str.replace("## COMPLETED FROM
THE QUEUE", ..., 1)` inserts at **line 230**, inside a dated note that merely mentions the heading,
not at the register on line 502. The resume state of 2026-09-12 warned about this trap for READING
("Slice from the heading line itself"); it is worse for WRITING, because a bad read returns a wrong
count while a bad write corrupts the file. Match the heading **line-exactly and assert it is
unique**, then verify by counting the entries back. The USNA fold hit it, caught it on the
verification read (count came back 155 with CRC still first), and reverted with `git checkout`
before committing.*

**Why this is written down rather than remembered:** the same defect class the runs keep
finding in the tooling - **a diagnostic that exists but never reaches the reader** - applied to
the process itself. The spread caveat lived only in console output, `best_year_dep` threw away
its own verdict string, and the fold lived only in whoever's head was holding the session.

## WRITING A BRIEF — one prohibition, earned the hard way
*Added 2026-09-07, from the CGNX run.*

**NEVER TELL A RUN WHICH GATE WILL BE BORING.** That brief said *"Q3/Q4 should be short. Do not
pad them."* **Q3 then carried the single sharpest finding in the file**: `[E4-29]` reads clean
in Cognex's 10-K - the word EBITDA does not appear - and **fires at full strength in the
furnished 8-K earnings releases**, where Adjusted EBITDA margin is the headline and the stated
milestone is *"25% Adjusted EBITDA margin, targeted on a run-rate basis by the end of 2026"*
against a 16.3% GAAP operating margin. The run's own words: **"telling a run which gate will be
boring is how a live flag gets scored clean."**

This is operator rule 9 turned on the brief-writer. A brief is a set of **hypotheses to be
refuted**, and an instruction to skim a gate is not a hypothesis - **it is a conclusion smuggled
in as advice**, and the run cannot refute it because it was told not to look. Brief the
EVIDENCE and the priors; never the expected verdict, and never the effort to spend.

**The companion, also from that run and now standing for every Q3:** pull the latest **8-K
EX-99.1 earnings release** before scoring `[E4-29]` and `[E4-22]`'s third flag. **A run that
reads only the annual report will score clean a company that has built its public narrative on
a non-GAAP metric.**
